subject: Clarify: where customer requests execute & subprocessor chain for US-only deployment
messages:
From: Aliya Hassan <aliya.hassan@medicore.com>
To: nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
Cc: brad.jensen@medicore.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: where customer requests execute & subprocessor chain for US-only deployment

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looked promising. Before we present to our security & procurement committees we need a concise summary of where requests from our app would execute and which subprocessors would touch any data for a US-only deployment. Two main asks: 

1) Execution footprint: if we choose US-only (no EU/APAC), which AWS regions/availability zones might be used? Do requests ever transit through non-US regions?

2) Subprocessors: we need a short list of 3rd parties involved in the request path (e.g., cloud provider, logging/metrics, key management). For each subprocessor can you include the role and whether they are contractually bound to Redwood with DPAs?

Also: any diagrams or one-page artifacts we can share with our InfoSec folks would be helpful.

Appreciate a tight reply — we have a Tuesday review meeting.

Best,
Aliya Hassan
Head of Security Programs
Medicore Health

(Attachment: requirements-template.xlsx)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Aliya Hassan <aliya.hassan@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, brad.jensen@medicore.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where customer requests execute & subprocessor chain for US-only deployment

Hi Aliya — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a compact breakdown below.

TL;DR
- Execution: For a US-only deployment we pin execution to US regions (primary: us-west-2; secondary failover: us-east-1). No intentional routing through EU/APAC.
- Transit: All control plane traffic (metrics, orchestration) can be configured to use the private control plane in your VPC for Private installs; hosted customers may see telemetry egress to our observability partner in the US only.
- Subprocessors: AWS (compute & storage), KeySafe KMS (managed keys), LogSpan (metrics/alerts), S3-compatible archival partner (for optional backups). All have DPAs or MCCs where relevant.

Detail (concise):
1) Execution footprint
- Default hosted US-only profile: model inference nodes run in us-west-2 (Oregon) as the primary. We maintain reserved capacity pools in us-west-2; cross-region failover uses us-east-1 (N. Virginia) but only when explicitly enabled by customer policy.
- Networking: requests are routed via our API gateway in the requested region; we do not route inference payloads through EU/APAC unless you opt into multi-region routing.
- Short caveat: some third-party infra callouts (e.g., global CDN for SDK downloads) are read-only and do not carry customer inference payloads.

2) Subprocessors (roles and contractual posture)
- Amazon Web Services (AWS) — compute, ephemeral block storage, S3 archival (where enabled). DPA in place; AWS is a processor. Regions: us-west-2, us-east-1 (failover).
- KeySafe Inc. — customer-managed KMS for Private installs or Redwood-managed key wrapping for hosted. DPA + SOC2 attestation. Keys can be customer-managed (recommended).
- LogSpan Analytics — aggregated telemetry/metric processing and alerting. PII-free by default; telemetry is pseudonymized and covered by a DPA. Can be disabled for Dedicated/Private.
- GlacierStore Partners — optional long-term backups/archives (S3-compatible). Used only if you enable retention-archive; DPA available.
- DocuSign (for contract flows) — limited to signature metadata; DPA available.

3) Data-at-rest and in-transit
- All inference payloads and model caches are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+). At rest encryption is enabled using AWS KMS (or KeySafe if you supply keys).

4) Deletion & retention notes
- Default hosted retention: short-lived inference artifacts are ephemeral (cached token/KV caches are purged per TTL). We retain logs and aggregated telemetry for 90 days by default; retention can be reduced to 30 days on request.
- Deletion path: when you request deletion we trigger removal from active stores and schedule clip/backup purges per the archival SLA (archival purge typically within 30 days; final garbage collection within 60 days depending on cross-region replication windows).

Attachments: I attached a one-page processing map (processing-diagram-v2.png) and a short checklist. I can also export a minimal evidence pack (SOC 2 pointer + DPAs) if that helps.

If helpful, Marissa can join to map this into your procurement checklist — Marissa, can you add the deletion SLA wording to the checklist?

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
(Attachment: processing-diagram-v2.png)

From: Aliya Hassan <aliya.hassan@medicore.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Brad Jensen <brad.jensen@medicore.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where customer requests execute & subprocessor chain for US-only deployment

Thanks — this is exactly the type of summary we need. A couple quick follow-ups from InfoSec: 

- Can you confirm cache lifetimes for model KV caches and whether any cached prompts are written to persistent storage? We need assurance that cached user prompts are neither archived nor included in long-term logs.
- For the hosted offering, is telemetry sent outside the US for anomaly detection? You mention LogSpan — where are their processing sites located?
- On deletion: please confirm whether deletion requests are irreversible and include a timestamped audit trail we can retain locally.

If you can add an explicit sentence we can paste into our procurement/ITAR slide that confirms "No inference payloads leave the US for our configured profile" that would be ideal.

Best,
Aliya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aliya Hassan <aliya.hassan@medicore.com>, nikhil.sharma@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: where customer requests execute & subprocessor chain for US-only deployment

Hi Aliya — looping in for the compliance wording you can include. Quick answers + proposed snippet for your slide.

- KV/cache behavior: Everything in the KV cache is ephemeral and stored on local NVMe attached to the inference node; we do not persist prompt text to long-term archival unless you explicitly enable "conversation logging". By default, cached items are TTL-based and cleared on eviction or node restart. We will add a note in the evidence pack clarifying no persistent storage of prompts.

- LogSpan processing location: LogSpan operates primary US processing clusters (us-east-1 & us-west-2). For hosted customers choosing US-only we route telemetry to LogSpan's US cluster; we can also suppress telemetry entirely for Dedicated/Private installs.

- Deletion and audit trail: Deletion is irreversible once completed. We provide a deletion confirmation with a timestamp and unique request id; we also log the deletion action in our audit events (audit events do not include the payload content). You can export the audit record and retain it locally.

Proposed slide sentence (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference (US-only profile) executes inference and related transient caching exclusively within AWS US regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover). No inference payloads are routed through EU or APAC regions under this configuration; telemetry processing for hosted customers is restricted to LogSpan's US clusters, and all subprocessors are bound by DPAs. Deletion requests result in irreversible purge of active and archival stores and are accompanied by a timestamped audit record"

Attachments: residency-deletion-checklist.pdf (one-page checklist + suggested procurement language).

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call with your team before Tuesday if you want to walk through the proof points.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(Attachment: residency-deletion-checklist.pdf)
